clue.text: Tiff means son needs caress

parts.note: to pat is to stroke gently, a caress

explanation.surface: A quarrel is settled when a boy just needs a cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a petty quarrel, the same as a tiff between friends.

clue.text: Collector beginning to hunt in very good old catalogue

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the word for very good

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, very good

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of hunt

parts.note: late means old or former
a list is a catalogue

explanation.surface: A collector starts hunting through a fine old catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good; H goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A philatelist is a stamp collector.

clue.text: Boss as best of the bunch?

definitions.meaning: the person in charge, informally the top dog
the fruit at the top of a bunch, read literally

explanation.surface: The boss is the pick of the crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Top banana is slang for the leader or boss, and literally the best fruit in a bunch.

clue.text: Imposer of taxes offers possibility to get bread back

parts.note: a chance is a possibility

indicators.note: back tells us the word for bread is read from right to left

parts.note: a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: A tax official offers a chance to get a loaf returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ROLL into LLOR. In Britain the Chancellor of the Exchequer is the minister who sets taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chancellor of the Exchequer is the UK finance minister who sets taxes each budget.

clue.text: Impudent youngster with pet on head is to be scolded

indicators.note: on head means the pet comes at the top of this down entry

parts.note: a cat is a pet
a chit is a cheeky young girl

explanation.surface: A cheeky child with a cat on her head is going to be told off.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on head' puts CAT above CHIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch it is an informal idiom meaning to get into trouble or be scolded.

clue.text: One of today's kids producing work with spiritual ending

definitions.meaning: a youngster of the present era
Michael Tippett's oratorio which uses African-American spirituals, ending with Deep River

explanation.surface: A modern child creates a piece of work that ends on a spiritual note.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a child of the present day, and the title of Tippett's 1941 oratorio featuring spirituals.

clue.text: Misbehaving tot is grabbed by companion

indicators.note: grabbed by means the next pieces are held inside the companion's letters

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: A naughty toddler is snatched up by a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' is a verb, as in tot up, giving ADD; CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: Caddish means behaving like a cad, dishonourably, which is misbehaving.

clue.text: Something for the bathroom or toilet a female held

indicators.note: held tells us the female letter is kept inside the other pieces

parts.note: loo is British slang for toilet

explanation.surface: A bathroom item, or a toilet held by a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofa is a fibrous sponge used for scrubbing in the bath.

clue.text: First sign of remorse —— a certain husband entering with flower

indicators.note: entering means the husband goes inside the other letters
first sign of means only the opening letter of remorse

parts.note: a certain one means a particular individual, giving one

explanation.surface: A husband shows remorse while coming in with a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is something that flows, a river: the Rhone. 'entering' puts H between R and ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower in crosswords is a river, something that flows, and the Rhone is a French river.

clue.text: Bowl with edge chipped off repaired or done away with

indicators.note: an edge chipped off means the bowl's word loses its final letter

parts.note: a dish is a bowl
patched means mended or repaired

explanation.surface: A chipped bowl is mended, or simply thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with edge chipped off' removes the last letter of DISH, leaving DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch someone is to kill them, so dispatched means done away with.

clue.text: Look back in river for explorer

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the river's name

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: back means the word for look is read in reverse

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look!

explanation.surface: Someone glances back along a river while searching for an explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LO into OL, which goes 'in' PO.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was the Venetian traveller and explorer who journeyed to China.

clue.text: Gangster in the money gets carriage

indicators.note: in places the gangster within the word for money

parts.note: cash is money
Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A mobster who is rich buys himself a carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A calash is a light, low-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding hood.

clue.text: Left needing help — seller of shares said to be exposed

parts.note: aid means help

indicators.note: said tells us the word is heard, not seen, giving a spelling that sounds alike

parts.note: a bear on the stock market sells shares expecting prices to fall

explanation.surface: A stock-market seller, left needing help, is shown up in public.
explanation.walkthrough: A BEAR sells shares expecting the price to fall; 'said' gives its sound-alike BARE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay something bare is to uncover it, so the phrase means revealed or exposed.

clue.text: Return to make speech after the break

indicators.note: after puts the speech following the break

parts.note: a rest is a break
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A politician goes back to give a speech after the holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A restoration is a return to a former state or of something to its owner.

clue.text: Woman in overalls

indicators.note: in tells us the name sits inside the word overalls

explanation.surface: A woman is dressed in overalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Vera is a woman's given name, as crosswords often use names for woman.

clue.text: One will clean things up, by gum!

definitions.text: One will clean things up, by gum!

parts.words: One will clean things up, by gum!
parts.note: by gum is a mock-northern exclamation, but read literally it is the place where a cleaning tool works: along the gums and teeth

explanation.definitionFit: A brush for teeth cleans them right up by the gums every morning.

clue.text: Criticise sloth with the French dropping speed

parts.note: to rap is to criticise sharply

indicators.note: dropping means the French article is removed from the word for sloth

parts.note: idleness is sloth
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone attacks laziness while giving up French in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes LE from IDLENESS, leaving IDNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapidness is quickness, the quality of moving at speed.

clue.text: Reject and offer conclusive evidence against having pocketed a penny

indicators.note: having pocketed means the word for refute holds the next letters inside it

parts.note: to disprove is to give evidence showing something false

explanation.surface: A defendant rejects the charge and refutes the claim that they stole a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having pocketed' puts A and P inside DISPROVE, after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: To disapprove of something is to reject it or hold an unfavourable opinion of it.

clue.text: Wrinkled fabric around bottom of the cloak

indicators.note: around means the fabric's letters surround the next letter

parts.note: plisse is a fabric with a puckered, wrinkled finish

indicators.note: in a down clue bottom of means the last letter of the

explanation.surface: Creased cloth is wrapped round the hem of a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom of' gives E, the last letter of 'the'; 'around' puts it inside PLISSE after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelisse is a long fur-lined cloak or mantle.

clue.text: Important fellow in play secures a pledge

indicators.note: secures means the fellow's name holds the letter inside it

parts.note: Ernest is the title figure of Wilde's The Importance of Being ...

explanation.surface: A leading man in a drama locks in a promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Important' looks like an adjective; it points to Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest, whose hero is Ernest.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest is a token payment or pledge made to secure a deal.

clue.text: Exhaust coming from part of ship

definitions.meaning: the raised deck at the stern of a sailing vessel

explanation.surface: Fumes come pouring out of part of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To poop is informal for to exhaust; the poop deck is the high stern deck of a ship.

clue.text: Pushchair in US street — wave!

parts.note: a roller is a long heavy wave breaking on the shore

explanation.surface: An American parent wheeling a pushchair down the street waves.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a baby's pushchair a stroller.

clue.text: Great performer enthralling India's capital, playing this?

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the performer's word holds the letter

parts.note: a star is a great performer

indicators.note: capital means the capital letter, the first one, of India

explanation.surface: A great musician enthrals India's capital, perhaps by playing this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' is not Delhi but the first letter of India, I.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is the long-necked Indian lute a great performer like Ravi Shankar played.

clue.text: Old coat shortened, taken up? It's capital!

indicators.note: in a down clue taken up means the letters are read from bottom to top
shortened means the coat's word loses its final letter

parts.note: a tabard is a short medieval coat worn over armour

explanation.surface: An old coat that has been taken up and shortened is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' cuts TABARD to TABAR; 'taken up' reverses it. 'It's capital!' plays on capital as an old word for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabat is the capital city of Morocco.

clue.text: Design again in single colour, green

parts.note: red is a single colour
green can mean raw, inexperienced or unripe

explanation.surface: An artist redoes a design using a single colour, green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' looks like the colour of the design; it means RAW, as in a green recruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraw a plan is to draw it once more, to design it anew.

clue.text: Valve container, earliest bit of electronics

parts.note: a tub is a container

indicators.note: earliest bit of means only the first letter of electronics is used

explanation.surface: An old radio valve sits in a box with the very first bits of electronics.
explanation.walkthrough: British English calls a thermionic valve a tube in the US sense, as in a vacuum tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A valve in old radios is the British name for an electronic vacuum tube.

clue.text: Twisted genius, father seen on reflection as a one-off

indicators.note: twisted tells us the letters of genius are bent into another order
on reflection means the word for father is mirrored, read right to left

parts.note: a sire is a father

explanation.surface: A warped genius father, thinking it over, sees himself as unique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted' rearranges GENIUS as SUIGEN; 'on reflection' turns SIRE into ERIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sui generis is Latin for of its own kind, describing something unique.

clue.text: Time without any work being done — entire term has been wasted

definitions.text: Time without any work being done

indicators.note: wasted means ruined or spoilt, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A pensioner laments that a whole school term was wasted without any work.
explanation.definitionFit: Retirement is the period of life after one stops working.

clue.text: Carol remarkable? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means half the letters of the synonym are dropped

parts.note: singular means remarkable or extraordinary

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a carol was remarkable and is told emphatically yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is a British exclamation meaning very much so; here it removes the second half of SINGULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To carol is to sing joyfully, so the verbs are synonyms.
